messages:
alex: Heads up — ACME reported a production regression after last night's registry migration. Their client calls \"summarize_doc\" but the platform routed to the old handler and returned a schema validation error. ticket TKT-4321.
acme-cs: Repro steps from our side: curl to /v1/toolcall with { \"tool\": \"summarize_doc\", \"args\": { \"text\": \"...\" } } -> 400 with body \"expected field 'max_tokens' in tool response\". Happens intermittently (~1/10 calls).
alex: grabbing logs now. can someone check resolver/cache state for acme tenant? :eyes:
nick: I can see the incoming request id=rcpt_01F7Z3. On the routing layer the resolver returned handler=\"summarize_docs_v0\" (legacy) at 2026-03-17T01:12:14Z. Registry shows alias mapping updated to \"summarize_doc -> summarize_docs_v1\" but edge caches still have v0.
sam: logs: 
```
route.debug: resolver=alias-resolver-2 tenant=acme alias=summarize_doc -> handler=summarize_docs_v0 source=cache ttl=3600
route.info: fallback to handler summarize_docs_v0 for request id rcpt_01F7Z3
```

jess: probably a rename propagation race. We ran the migration that replaced v0 with v1 and added casefolded aliases. Some caches (edge and client sdk caches) weren't invalidated. That explains intermittent calls.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: registry-migration v2026-03-16 completed. Cache invalidation job queued.
sam: repro answer: if client sets header X-Client-Cache: stale then it hits the old mapping, otherwise it gets v1. Looks like some SDKs ship with a persistent alias->handler cache that wasn't purged by the migration.
acme-cs: any ETA? This is impacting customers with short timeout budgets.
sre-lead: short term mitigation: purge alias cache on the public edge for tenant acme and issue a quick client SDK patch to drop local alias cache on next startup. I'll run a cache flush now.
alex: steps to reproduce (internal):
1) run `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{"tool":"summarize_doc","args":{"text":"hello"}}'` repeatedly (~20 reqs)
2) observe some responses 200 from summarize_docs_v1 and some 400 from summarize_docs_v0 with schema mismatch.
3) server headers: `x-resolver-source: cache` for the 400s.
nick: root cause hypothesis: registry rename wrote new canonical name but didn't bump the cache key namespace in the alias-resolver. The casefolding normalization meant v1 and V1 (capital V) looked equivalent in some places but not when clients used byte-preserving alias. Migration script assumed eventual consistency but caches are sticky for 1h.
jess: proposed fixes:
- immediate: purge edge alias caches for affected tenants (done by SRE).
- short: push client SDK patch to invalidate local alias cache on token refresh.
- long: change migration to write a tombstone entry that forces resolver miss for 5m before new alias appears, so no mixed-state routing.
sre-lead: purge started at 2026-03-17T01:18Z. monitoring: error rate for toolcall (summarize_doc) down from 7% -> 0.2% in 15m.
acme-cs: Thanks team — ACME confirms errors dropped. They still saw a few failures while their client restarted, but all good now. :thumbsup:
alex: follow-ups: create runbook note for rename migrations (include tombstone step), track SDK patch rollout, close TKT-4321 once SDK has update. Assign to sam/jess.
nick: logging note — capture `x-resolver-source` and alias->handler mapping in toolcall traces for 48h after future renames to speed triage.
alex: awesome. closing loop here. :white_check_mark:
